prompt:
AUDIO PROFILE
Cleo: a young woman software developer in her mid twenties. Soft, natural, conversational voice. Real and understated, never cartoonish.
Claude: a young man's voice. Calm, warm and gently dry-witted, never theatrical. Few words.

THE SCENE, END TO END
Evening at her desk. After three hours Cleo's code finally works; she asks Claude, a small AI companion on her desk, to tidy it before she commits. His refactor breaks everything, she never committed, but he saved a checkpoint.

LINE BY LINE
1. Cleo, relieved, proud, a little tired.
2. Claude, pleased with himself.
3. Cleo, rising panic.
4. Claude, calm, admiring his own work.
5. Cleo, firm, reaching for control.
6. Claude, innocent.
7. Cleo, the realization arriving mid-sentence.
8. Claude, gentle, dry.
9. Cleo, defensive, embarrassed.
10. Cleo, small, scared.
11. Claude, calm and reassuring.
12. Cleo, pure joy and relief.
13. Cleo, urgent whisper, then decisive.
14. Claude, hopeful, polite.
15. Cleo, breezy, confident now.
16. Claude, deadpan.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES
A natural, conversational pace, like two friends at a desk; not rushed, not slow. Let the jokes land with a short beat before the dry lines. Leave a short beat at every [medium pause] and at every "..."; never read the bracketed tags aloud. Speak every word of the dialogue exactly as written, nothing added.
turns: Claude, it finally works. Three hours. Just clean it up so I can commit.
Done. I merged your helpers, renamed every variable, and rewrote the state logic.
Why is my whole screen red?
It's broken right now. But the architecture is gorgeous.
Forget gorgeous. I'm going back to my last commit.
The one from... three hours ago.
Because you wouldn't commit until the code was pretty.
Nineteen console logs, Claude. What if someone saw? [medium pause] So my working code is just... gone?
Not quite. I saved a checkpoint before I touched anything. Rewinding now.
My ugly code! It's alive! [medium pause] Nobody move. I'm committing this hideous mess.
Now that it's safe... may I make it gorgeous?
Go ahead. If you break it, I'll just roll it back.
I liked you better when you panicked.
